# ViewportScaler

[Toolkit](README.md) · `DotGame.Toolkit.Graphics` · class

```csharp
public sealed class ViewportScaler
```

Draws a game designed for one size on a screen of any size: tell it the size you designed for and draw in those coordinates, whatever the window or device.

## Example

```csharp
scaler.Update(this.ClientBounds);
using var scissor = this.Graphics.UseScissor(scaler.Viewport);   // Keeps Fit's bars clear
using (spriteBatch.Begin(scaler.Transform))
{
    spriteBatch.Draw(background, Vector2.Zero, Color.White);
}

var pointer = scaler.ScreenToDesign(e.Position); ```

## Constructors

```csharp
public ViewportScaler(Vector2Int designSize, ViewportScaleMode mode = ViewportScaleMode.Fit)
```

Types: [`Vector2Int`](https://github.com/hotchaipro/DotGame.Framework/blob/main/docs/api/Framework/Vector2Int.md), [`ViewportScaleMode`](ViewportScaleMode.md)

Makes a scaler for the size you designed for.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `designSize` | The size you draw in. |
| `mode` | How that fits onto the screen. |

**Throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`:** The size isn't positive.

### Transform

```csharp
public Matrix3x2 Transform { get; }
```

Gets the transform from design coordinates to the screen, for `SpriteBatch.Begin`.

### Viewport

```csharp
public RectangleInt Viewport { get; }
```

Types: [`RectangleInt`](https://github.com/hotchaipro/DotGame.Framework/blob/main/docs/api/Framework/RectangleInt.md)

Gets the part of the screen the game draws in, clipped to the screen: the area between [`ViewportScaleMode.Fit`](ViewportScaleMode.md#fit)'s bars. Use it as the scissor rectangle to keep them clear.

### VisibleBounds

```csharp
public Rectangle VisibleBounds { get; }
```

Types: [`Rectangle`](https://github.com/hotchaipro/DotGame.Framework/blob/main/docs/api/Framework/Rectangle.md)

Gets the part of the design coordinates that's on screen, for laying out to the edges of the screen and for leaving out what can't be seen. It's the whole design with [`ViewportScaleMode.Fit`](ViewportScaleMode.md#fit), less of it with [`ViewportScaleMode.Fill`](ViewportScaleMode.md#fill), and more of it with [`ViewportScaleMode.Expand`](ViewportScaleMode.md#expand), from the design's top left going on below and to the right.
